title: Citizenship voting appeal, energy taxes and Storm Adam
summary:
Spain's Ombudsman is seeking an urgent restoration of voting rights for citizens naturalised under the Ley de Nietos. We cover election alliances, energy taxes, mortgages and parental benefits, plus Storm Adam's forecast heavy rain.

Enjoying Spain Daily? Support us: https://buymeacoffee.com/spanified

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: Will citizens naturalised under the Ley de Nietos get to vote on November twenty-ninth? An urgent court appeal could decide.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: The Ombudsman wants their voting suspension lifted immediately. The Constitutional Court now has that request.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: Good morning! It's Saturday, the seventeenth of October, and this is Spain Daily, from Spanified dot com!

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: I'm Inna. We've got different outcomes for fuel and electricity taxes, and heavy rain forecast as Storm Adam arrives.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: And I'm Dima. First, the Ley de Nietos voting appeal, with the general election approaching.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: El Mundo reports that Spain's Ombudsman asked the Constitutional Court on October sixteenth to urgently lift a voting suspension. It affects citizens naturalised under the Ley de Nietos, a citizenship route for descendants of Spaniards. The Supreme Court upheld the suspension on October twelfth. The pending appeal will determine whether affected citizens can vote in the November twenty-ninth general election.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: Inna, how urgent is the request? Does the Ombudsman want the court to act before hearing everyone involved?

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: That's what he's asking. An immediate lifting of the suspension, without first hearing the affected parties.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: And the Ombudsman, Spain's rights watchdog, stepped in after receiving requests from affected people?

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: From individuals and organisations. The State Legal Service had concluded it couldn't legally bring its own constitutional rights appeal. oh I see

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: For people affected, that's a very personal question hanging over election day: whether they'll be able to cast their ballot.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: And the Supreme Court ruling opened another route for participation: affected people can join the case and submit arguments.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: Staying with the election, El Mundo reports that the Socialist Party and several left-wing and regional parties agreed joint Senate lists. They'll stand under 'Senado de Progreso', aiming to challenge the People's Party's previous absolute majority. Podemos remains outside the agreement, with its Senate candidacy unclear.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: So the parties are pooling support for the Senate, the upper parliamentary chamber. Who's joining the Socialists?

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: Sumar and regional groups are among the partners. That gives several parties a shared route to challenging that majority.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: For the wider election, Europa Press reports that Frente Amplio registered its nationwide coalition without Podemos after talks failed. They'll compete separately in most constituencies. Joint lists survived only in the Canary Islands and the Valencian Community.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: Ah, those regional exceptions matter. Someone voting in Valencia will face a different arrangement from voters in most constituencies.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: And elsewhere, competing lists could divide left-wing support. That can affect how seats are distributed.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: There's a candidate change too. Europa Press reports that Socialist spokesperson Montse Mínguez announced her departure from politics on October sixteenth. Following controversy over her partner's property holdings, she's giving up all party posts and won't seek re-election to Congress. She had been due to lead the party's list for Lleida, in Catalonia.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: That's a lead candidacy to replace while the election is already approaching.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: And a spokesperson's role too. The party has both a local list and a national position to address.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: On household costs, El Diario reports that Congress's standing committee validated an extension of fuel tax cuts. Fuel discounts remain until December, alongside a gas tariff cap for vulnerable households. The People's Party, Socialists, Sumar and other parties backed the decree. Vox voted against.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: Oh, some continuity for drivers. But the gas protection is aimed at vulnerable households, rather than every household?

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: That's the group covered by the cap. right The extension keeps that protection in place heading into winter.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: Electricity has a different outcome. El Mundo reports that electricity VAT stays at twenty-one percent. September's annual electricity inflation fell below the plan's trigger of more than fifteen percent. So the planned cuts to VAT and electricity tax don't kick in, and households miss the expected savings on November bills.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: Huh. Electricity prices have kept rising, but the tax relief depends on how fast they rise.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: Which leaves households paying full VAT on a rising bill, while the fuel tax discounts continue.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: El Diario reports that Spain blocked EU summit wording aimed at its migrant regularisation process, which grants legal status. Portugal, Luxembourg and France backed Spain. Denmark, Poland and Italy wanted language opposing measures they argued could attract more irregular migration. The final conclusions don't mention Spain's migration management.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: What did the countries manage to agree on in the final wording?

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: Only a reference to a strategic debate on the EU's overall migration approach. Spain's process avoided criticism in those conclusions.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: El Confidencial reports that Eurostat confirmed eurozone annual inflation reached three point eight percent in September, a three-year high. Fresh food inflation accelerated too. The figures add pressure on the European Central Bank over interest rates.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: So this reaches beyond the shopping basket. People with variable mortgages have another reason to follow those rate decisions.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: Central bank rates can influence Euribor, the benchmark many variable mortgages follow. mhm That's how inflation can reach mortgage costs.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: And mortgage borrowing remains substantial. Expansión reports that Spain's mortgage association expects half a million loans this year, matching last year. The average loan has risen to about a hundred and eighty-one thousand euros. Banks are tightening offers as Euribor rises, and fixed-rate loans are gaining appeal. Bankers expect lending to cool next year.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: Oof. A strong lending total doesn't make the individual purchase easier when buyers need larger loans.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: Especially with offers tightening. Fixed-rate loans are attracting borrowers looking for stable payments.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: For this weekend, Europa Press reports that Aemet forecasts very heavy, persistent showers from today. Parts of Spain's Mediterranean coast and the Balearic Islands are affected, with storms expected in Levante, eastern Spain. Aemet has named the system Adam, the season's first high-impact DANA, a weather system associated with intense rain.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: Persistent rain is the concern here, not just a passing shower. Disruption is expected in Levante and the Balearics.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: Check Aemet's official alerts for your area this weekend, especially along the affected Mediterranean coast and in the islands.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: In brief, Expansión reports that Galicia's draft budget for next year proposes a quarter-percentage-point income tax cut across four bands. The Galician Parliament must approve the proposal. The cuts would apply retroactively from January.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: On a more serious note, El Diario reports that thousands marched in Madrid on October sixteenth during the indefinite teachers' strike. Teachers want a six-hundred-euro pay rise, smaller classes and fewer teaching hours. The strike covers infant through secondary schools, disrupting schooling for families.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: In hospital supply news, El Mundo reports that Curaleaf expects to distribute two registered cannabis preparations to fifty Spanish hospitals. Delivery is expected by the end of October. Hospital pharmacies would use the preparations as raw materials to make medicines for patients.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: And Veinte Minutos reports that domestic workers now have equal access to Social Security birth, adoption and childcare benefits. Payments equal a hundred percent of the earnings base for the month before leave begins. Workers must be registered and meet age-based contribution requirements. Those under twenty-one need no prior contributions.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: That's income protection during leave for domestic workers. Registration and contribution history matter when applying.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: And younger workers can qualify without having built up a contribution record.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: Our takeaway: the voting appeal is pending, fuel relief continues, and Storm Adam makes local weather alerts especially relevant this weekend.

segments.body: Thanks for spending part of your Saturday with us. We're glad you're listening.
